slides.title: Session JWT
slides.subtitle: Sign one request's Session JWT with a delegated key, and keep it out of the model
slides.notes: Every request to a company carries a Session JWT in the Poppy-Session header. It names the Session and the User, and it covers that one request. This example signs a real one, verifies it, and changes each thing it covers to show the refusal.

slides.title: Why a JWT per request
slides.statement: An access token says **which account**. The Session JWT says **which Session, which User, and this request**.
slides.notes: The company joins the two on each request. Signed out, the request carries the Session JWT alone. Signed in, it carries an access token too, and the JWT's ath claim holds the token's hash. A copied access token is refused without a Session header from the agent's key. The JWT never grants account access by itself.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Your host, trusted"] direction TB H["PAP host"] -- "sign this request" --> K["Reactor Session signer
holds the delegated keys"] end subgraph CO["Company"] direction TB A["Company API
verifies the Session header"] -- "record jti" --> X[("Replay cache")] end HOST -- "request, Poppy-Session, Bearer token" --> CO HOST -. "policy booleans only" .-> M
slides.caption: The key never leaves the Session signer; the model gets yes-or-no evidence, nothing more.
slides.notes: The host asks for a Session JWT covering one request. The Reactor Session signer signs it with a delegated key, without ever giving the key out, and puts the delegation that vouches for the key in the JWT's header as pap_dlg. The company verifies the delegation against the agent's jwks_uri, then the JWT against the delegated key. A company may also reject a reused jti, as the reference companies do. Off to the side, the model: all it ever receives from this exchange is yes-or-no evidence about the policy.

slides.title: What a Session JWT covers

rows.label: htm, htu
values: This request, without query or fragment

rows.label: iat, jti
values: Now, and one use where the company checks

slides.notes: Each claim narrows where the JWT works. The audience ties it to one company, the sid and sub to one Session and User, the method and URL to one request target. The token hash ties it to the token without putting the token in the JWT, and is absent when there is no token. The iat keeps it fresh, and the jti lets a company refuse a second use.

slides.title: First use, then a replay
slides.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as PAP host
  participant C as Company API
  participant X as Replay cache
  H->>C: Request, Poppy-Session, token
  C->>C: Delegation, signature, claims
  C->>X: Record jti
  X-->>C: Accepted
  C-->>H: API response
  H->>C: Same Session JWT again
  C->>X: Record jti
  X-->>C: Already seen
  C-->>H: 400 invalid_session
slides.notes: The first time, the company verifies the delegation, the signature and the claims, records the jti atomically, and the request goes through. The same JWT a second time is already in the cache, so the company answers 400 with invalid_session. Rejecting a reused jti is a company's choice; the reference companies do it.

slides.title: What the example proves
items: A new `jti` and Session JWT for every attempt, retry and redirect
`htm`, `htu` and `aud` stop reuse on another request or at another company
`ath` binds the JWT to the token without embedding it
Each User ID has its own delegated key
Where a company rejects replays, the check is **atomic** across its fleet
slides.notes: Retries and redirects always get a new JWT. Each User ID at a company has its own delegated key, so a key's thumbprint names one User at one company. And a company that rejects replays must make the check atomic across every server it runs, or a replay could slip through on another node.

slides.title: What the model sees

left.heading: Visible
items: Policy booleans: method, URL, token and company bound

right.heading: Never
items: The Session JWT or the token
The keys, the Session ID, the User ID

slides.notes: The tool returns only yes-or-no evidence about the policy. The Session JWT, the delegation, the token, the keys and the identifiers stay in host code.
